acquisition method: data-dependent acquisition selected the top 10 most abundant precursor ions for tandem mass spectrometry
alkylation reagent: alkylated with idoacetamide followed by trypsin digestion
cleavage agent: alkylated with idoacetamide followed by trypsin digestion on S-Trap micro
collision energy: by HCD fragmentation using an isolation width of 1.2 m/z, normalized collision energy of 30, and a resolution of 30,000.
enrichment method: the treated and clicked cell lysates were subjected to streptavidin agarose precipitation, and the bound proteins were analyzed using Western blot analyses.
fragmentation method: selected the top 10 most abundant precursor ions for tandem mass spectrometry by HCD fragmentation
instrument: delivered to a Q-Exactive HF mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific)
ionization type: delivered to a Q-Exactive HF mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific) using electrospray ionization
labeling: The relative abundance of each protein was quantified by label-free spectra counting (Table S2).
precursor tolerance: the monoisotopic parent ion mass tolerance set to 1.25 Da
fragment tolerance: the monoisotopic fragment ion mass tolerance set at 0.02 Da.
ptm: static modification of +57.02146 Da on cysteine residues; variable modification of +15.9949 Da on methionine residues
A static modification of +57.02146 Da was added to all cysteine residues and a variable modification of +15.9949 Da on methionine residues.
reduction reagent: Samples were reduced with dithiothreitol and alkylated with idoacetamide
